dossier.public_summary: The 5.95-day dip occurs every stellar rotation and is accompanied by a strong fifty-thousand-PPM spot signal and a phase curve about half as deep as the dips. Its 4-hour grazing shape does not match the star and there is a faint second dip halfway around the orbit. Together this points to the star's own spotted variability and/or a small stellar companion eclipsing it, not a planet.

reasons.why: Large out-of-transit swing at the 5.95 d period, ~half the transit depth, with high chi2 indicates spots or a close stellar companion, not a planet.
Dip period equals the stellar rotation period (1.02 x) on a strongly spotted (VARIABLE) K dwarf, supporting the phase curve as stellar variability rather than a transit.

Significant secondary eclipse at half-orbit with depth 29% of primary and comparable to best brightening; odd-even alone is consistent but combined with secondary and phase curve favours stellar eclipses over a planet.
reasons.value: odd_even diff_sigma 0.4977, secondary snr 4.643 at phase 0.5012, depth_over_dip 0.2923, best_brightening_snr 6.722

reasons.why: Transit is much longer than central for a 0.76 Rsun star and very grazing (b 0.922), giving negative density ratio and large penalty, inconsistent with a normal planet transit.
reasons.value: duration ratio 1.51, observed_h 4 vs central_h 2.65, fit_b 0.9223, star_density_penalty 141.5, fit_log_density_ratio -2.144

reasons.why: Dip is on target, ruling out a blended neighbour within one pixel (21 arcsec), so the binary/variability must be on the target itself.
